headline: Denmark's culture minister is proposing a law to ban sharing realistic AI copies of a person's face or voice without consent.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: a national government's concrete bill on deepfakes, though still subject to parliament.
importance_line: People in Denmark would gain a legal right against realistic fake copies of their face and voice, which matters to artists and public figures and to platforms that would have to remove such content, but the bill still needs parliament and the line between satire and unlawful fakes would be left to courts.
summary: Reuters reports that Danish Culture Minister Zenia Stampe planned to propose a bill on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that would make it illegal to digitally copy and share realistic imitations of a person's looks and voice, mainly to push tech companies to remove manipulated content fast. Parody, satire and work that criticises those in power would be exempt, and Stampe hopes the law takes effect around the turn of the year, subject to parliamentary approval.
